about: Places whose truth is known, and what the viewer's rules should say about them. check_rules.py scores the rules against this file. Add a case whenever a place has been looked at closely: what is true there (truth), how it is known (source), and the checks that follow from it. Dates are nights (YYYY-MM-DD); lat/lon in degrees.

checks.event: the change log (product) has a change within within_km of the place starting on `on` (give or take `days`, default 1), of kind (one, or a list: a light going out reads off or dimmer) and cause when given
checks.events_at_most: no change in the log within within_km of the place (between from and to, when given) is rated above `level` (weak < medium < strong), and none has a cause in not_cause
checks.profile: the place's own year (a window of size_km): its shape (one of `shape`), whether it varies, whether it is active, its consistency (at least consistency_min, at most consistency_max), and for a step its direction (1 up, -1 down) and when (between when_from and when_to)
checks.related: what the related-places question answers for the place on `night`: mode (event: where else it happened; corr: what moves with it), change (night or step), way (up or down), stable, chose (night: the place's own series; detected: a change the list found inside it), and how unusual nearby (local_ratio_min)

cases.name: fire east of Jerusalem
cases.truth: One night, 28 Jul 2026: the lights jump about x3.4 (x8 in the 750 m around it) and TEMPER sees heat at the same place that night only. A fire, back to normal the next night.
cases.source: Seen in the data on 26 Oct 2026 (the user asked why 'where else' found no change there).

cases.name: Ashdod port lights
cases.truth: Bright port lights that dip for a single night at a single pixel now and then. No fire, and no real change in the lights.
cases.source: The user's review on 26 Oct 2026: weak SWIR, no measured temperature, and the DNB dips do not look like real changes.

cases.name: on/off light south-west of Riyadh
cases.truth: A light of about 20 nW that flickers: short dips of 2-3 nights (Nov 2025, Apr 2026) and one-pixel brightenings are its usual behaviour, not changes. From 15 Oct 2026 it is off (about 2 nW) on most nights, after 2.5 months steady: that one is a real change.
cases.source: The user's question on 26 Oct 2026; its nights read on 26-27 Oct 2026 (Aug-Oct at the pixel: 13-35 nW until 4 Oct, then 1-3 nW on 6 of 8 nights).

cases.name: Sharurah dims in September
cases.truth: The lights step down to about half around 10-15 Sep 2026 and stay there; several blocks around it step down at the same time.
cases.source: Seen in the data on 26 Oct 2026 (the user asked about a peak on 14 Sep under clouds).

cases.name: Riyadh centre
cases.truth: A large city whose lights are steady all year.
cases.source: Common knowledge; its year read on 26 Oct 2026.

cases.name: Abqaiq oil processing
cases.truth: A large oil and gas plant: steady lights, and gas flares that TEMPER sees burning on nearly every night.
cases.source: Common knowledge (Saudi Aramco's Abqaiq plant); its year read on 26 Oct 2026.

cases.name: Jubail flare surge
cases.truth: A gas flare 1.7 km west-north-west burns on most nights. On 25 Oct 2026 (the last night in the data) it burned about x4 its usual and its heat reached this usually cold pixel (x24 there): one night of a bigger flame, ordinary for the flare itself (+2.7 s.d.; it was twice as strong on 5 Oct). The same pixel lit this way on 17 Dec 2025 and 5 Oct 2026.
cases.source: The user's question on 27 Oct 2026: the list showed 'strengthened · flame · 25 Oct', and related places from the kept area said there was no change.

cases.name: Rub' al Khali desert
cases.truth: Empty desert: no lights and no heat.
